verdict.rationale: Qdrant's security docs describe three API key types, including read-only keys for query-only consumers and granular access keys scoped per collection for read or write. That is a first-party least-privilege credential capability an agent can be given. The evidence does not show how these keys are issued or minted (for example token generation, expiry or revocation), and no hands-on report confirms the scoping works in practice. missing for 10: documented issuance/minting workflow for scoped keys, expiry and revocation controls, finer-grained scopes beyond per-collection read/write, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Qdrant supports three types of API key: **Admin API Key**... **Read-Only API Key**... **Granular Access API Keys**
read-only API keys for query-only consumers and granular access API keys with per-collection read/write scoping
